facts.statement: The genus Yamaceratops was described by P. J. Makovicky and M. A. Norell in September 2006.
facts.quote: The type species, Yamaceratops dorngobiensis, was described by P. J. Makovicky and M. A. Norell in September, 2006.

facts.statement: Fossils of Yamaceratops have been found in the Javkhlant Formation.
facts.quote: The Yamaceratops fossil material is known from the Javkhlant Formation.

facts.statement: Yamaceratops lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Mongolia.
facts.quote: Yamaceratops is a genus of primitive ceratopsian that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Mongolia.

facts.statement: Yamaceratops was a small dinosaur estimated to be 50 cm long and weigh around 2 kg.
facts.quote: It was a relatively small dinosaur, with an estimated length of 50 cm and weighing around 2 kg.

facts.statement: Yamaceratops had a wide, thick skull ending in a parrot-like beak used to cut ferns, cycads, and conifers, which it then chewed with posterior teeth.
facts.quote: Su cráneo, ancho y grueso, terminaba en un pico similar al de los loros, con el cual cortaba los helechos, cicádeas y coníferas de la que se alimentaba, para luego masticarlos con los dientes posteriores.

facts.statement: A fossilized embryo found in an ornithischian eggshell was initially referred to Yamaceratops in 2008 but was reidentified as a bird embryo in 2015.
facts.quote: A fossilized embryo found within an ornithischian eggshell from sediments where Yamaceratops is common, was referred to this genus in 2008. However, it was reidentified as a bird embryo in 2015.

facts.statement: A juvenile Yamaceratops specimen was estimated to be about three years old and weigh 1.2 kg.
facts.quote: This immature individual was approximately three years old, with an estimated body mass of 1.2 kg.

facts.statement: Examination of Yamaceratops fossils suggests its frill was not used for display and hints at a complex evolutionary history for ceratopsian frills.
facts.quote: Examination of the frill of Yamaceratops has convinced the authors that the frill was not used for display, and that the fossils "hint at a more complex evolutionary history for ceratopsian frills".

facts.statement: Yamaceratops lived from the Santonian to the Campanian stages, between 85.7 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Campanian (85.7 to 72.2 million years ago)
